note: Severities from the sponsor's CANTINA.md fix log, not the official PDF. #546/#522 and #63/#788 share one fix each.

findings.title: Native ETH removeLiquidity reentrancy lets LP swap against withdrawn stale reserves
findings.root_cause: removeLiquidity sends native ETH before burning shares and lowering reserves, so the ETH callback can re-enter and swap against the stale, still-large reserves.

findings.title: quoteZapIn underestimates shares, undermining slippage protection
findings.root_cause: The quote computes LP shares from pre-balancing-swap balances while sizing the deposit for post-swap balances, so it reads low and the user's minShares tolerance is far weaker than intended.

findings.title: Reachable 4-token pool states allow zero-input exact-output reserve extraction
findings.root_cause: In reachable heavily imbalanced states, the exact-output required-input calculation rounds down to zero, so tokens leave the pool for no input.

findings.title: Zero-fee exact-input round trips can extract reserves through StableSwap rounding asymmetry
findings.root_cause: Pools may be deployed with a 0% LP fee, removing the retained-fee floor, so price-neutral round trips skim reserves through rounding.

findings.title: Zero LP fee deployment allows a single exact-input swap to drain an output reserve, permanently bricking addLiquidity
findings.root_cause: Same root as #546: with no net LP fee left in reserves (0% LP fee, or hook+protocol cut equal to 100% of it), one swap can drive a reserve to zero and brick deposits and swaps.

findings.title: StableSwapZapIn._calculateSwapAmount overshoots target ratio in 3+ token pools, causing up to ~17% LP-share loss
findings.root_cause: A missing divisor in the balancing-swap sizing overshoots the target in pools of 3+ tokens, forcing extra fee-paying corrective swaps.

findings.title: Asymmetric exact-output math enables systemic fee evasion and LP yield loss
findings.root_cause: The exact-output fee is added on top of the trade cost rather than grossed up, so exact-output swaps pay less fee than the equivalent exact-input swap.

findings.title: StableSwap invariant overflow causes persistent swap DoS in imbalanced pools
findings.root_cause: Invariant computation overflows at reachable imbalanced reserve states, and every swap recomputes the invariant first, so all swaps revert.

findings.title: Low-amp pools can be pushed into non-convergent reserve states that brick swaps
findings.root_cause: Nothing stops swaps or deposits from leaving a low-amplification pool in a state where the invariant iteration does not converge, after which every swap reverts.

findings.title: Integer rounding in 3-token geometricMean leads to mispriced initial invariant and capital loss for LPs
findings.root_cause: The geometric mean takes the cube root of each balance separately and multiplies, rounding down three times and undervaluing the first LP's deposit.

findings.title: zapIn passes zero slippage to internal addLiquidity / swaps, enabling sandwich attacks
findings.root_cause: The internal balancing swaps run with no per-swap minimum output, so adverse moves mid-zap are only caught (loosely) by the final minShares check.

findings.title: Low-decimal exact-output swaps can withdraw LP reserves for zero input
findings.root_cause: When pairing a 0-6 decimal token with an 18-decimal token, the required input is rounded down when descaled and can reach zero.
